subject: POC Kickoff: Stakeholder intros, prompt review & load run scheduling

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-07-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: POC kickoff — two short items to align before we book

Hi Samantha and Liam,

Thanks again for confirming interest in a hands-on POC. Quick note with two asks before we lock calendar time:

1) Stakeholder roster — who should we invite for the kickoff (technical, product owner, security)? We typically keep the first call to 45 minutes for intros and alignment, then schedule a 3-hour lab slot for prompt review + routing/load trials.

2) Access checklist — see attached Network-Access-Checklist.xlsx. Can you confirm whether you have a corporate VPN restriction that would block our test runner? If so, we’ll work through a temporary CIDR or live Share session.

Proposed windows (PST):
- Wed Jul 15, 10:00–10:45 (kickoff) + Thu Jul 16, 09:00–12:00 (hands-on)
- Thu Jul 16, 14:00–14:45 (kickoff) + Fri Jul 17, 09:00–12:00 (hands-on)

If none of those work, tell us 2–3 times that do and we’ll adapt. I’ve cc’d Monica (CS lead) and Vivek (solutions engineer) so they can prep the prompt set and routing plan.

Attached: POC-Runbook-v0.9.pdf (draft agenda + success criteria), Network-Access-Checklist.xlsx

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: POC kickoff — two short items to align before we book

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear windows. Quick answers:

- Stakeholders: I’ll invite myself (Samantha — Head of Data Ops), Liam (CTO), Jordan Kim (Platform Eng) and our Security lead (TBD — I’ll confirm name tomorrow). We prefer one technical rep and one decision-maker on the kickoff.
- Network: We do have restrictive egress rules. Jordan will work through the checklist and confirm CIDR exceptions. If that’s slow, we’re fine with a shared remote session for the hands-on portion.

Both proposed kickoff windows look OK; prefer Wed Jul 15 at 10:00 PST. The 3-hour lab slot Thu Jul 16 09:00–12:00 also looks good.

Can you send an invite with dial-in and a short agenda? Also please add any prework we should complete before Thu (prompt list, sample data constraints).

Samantha

Subject: Re: POC kickoff — two short items to align before we book

Thanks — locking Wed Jul 15 10:00–10:45 PST for kickoff. I’ll send a calendar invite shortly.

A few logistics/actions for our side and yours:
- Monica: will prepare a 10-min one-slide success criteria and a one-page routing overview.
- Vivek: will prep prompt-review artifacts and a short sample prompt set (we’ll ask you to flag any sensitive fields).
- Samantha/Jordan: please review the Network-Access-Checklist so we’re unblocked for the Thu hands-on slot. If you prefer an alternate connectivity approach (shared session + screen), let us know.

Prework for Thu’s hands-on (short list):
- Confirm 1–2 prompt flows you want us to prioritize (e.g., customer support routing, doc summarization, ranking).
- A sanitized sample dataset (CSV or JSONL) < 2MB or a small synthetic example with the same schema.
- Any blacklisted tokens or sensitive PHI markers to avoid.

I’ve created a provisional calendar event and included a short agenda and links: kickoff 15 Jul 10:00–10:45 PST (intro + success criteria), hands-on 16 Jul 09:00–12:00 PST (prompt review, routing test, load ramp). Event link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=example_invite_id

If you need to shift the hands-on to Fri we can — but Thu is preferred to keep momentum.

Camila

--

Quick debrief from our side after the kickoff — thanks for the clear agenda. Two notes that matter for the hands-on:
1) We want to run a routing test that simulates 200 rps for 30 minutes (roughly to validate autoscaling / KV cache behavior). Can you confirm Redwood’s suggested batching/quantization settings for that run?
2) Jordan will confirm CIDR exceptions by end of day Thu; if that’s delayed we want to fallback to a secure screen-share + session recording approach.

We’ll upload a small sanitized dataset by EOD Thu and have our Platform Eng available for the hands-on. Looking forward — Liam
